# Event Messaging Library (`src/common/msging`)

This is the design document for msging infra

**Scope:** The shared transport library between the collector (producer side) and the
ingest service (server side). It owns reliable at-least-once delivery of event envelopes
(system architecture §5) and the producer registration/auth handshake (§7.1, §18.1).
It does **not** own event semantics: payloads are opaque to this library.

---

questions.question: How far should the x86 purge go? (I'd stage it — each stage is safe to stop at.)

options.label: All three, staged and verified (Recommended)
options.description: Stage 1: rebuild framework Python 3.12 site-packages natively (fixes the real breakage, ~5 min). Stage 2: `brew bundle dump` the Intel list, reinstall all 112 missing formulae under /opt/homebrew, verify every binary resolves to /opt/homebrew, THEN remove /usr/local. Stage 3: replace x86 anaconda3 with an arm64 miniconda, re-creating your envs. I stop for your OK between stages.

options.label: Homebrew + framework Python only
options.description: Stages 1 and 2. Reclaims ~4.9 GB and removes every x86 Python interpreter. Leaves ~/anaconda3 (11 GB, x86) alone — it keeps working under Rosetta and stays out of your way unless you activate it.

options.label: Framework Python 3.12 only
options.description: Stage 1 only. Purges the 88 x86 .so files from the shared site-packages and reinstalls them arm64-native. Fixes what actually broke, touches nothing else. The Intel brew and anaconda x86 trees stay.

options.label: Just show me the plan
options.description: I produce a fully-vetted, commented shell script for all three stages with verification gates and rollback notes, and delete nothing myself. You run it when you're ready.

questions.question: For the destructive removals (rm -rf of /usr/local/Cellar, ~/anaconda3), how do you want them handled?

options.label: Move aside first, delete later (Recommended)
options.description: Rename to /usr/local/Cellar.x86-old and ~/anaconda3.x86-old, verify everything still works for a few days, then you delete them yourself. Fully reversible; costs disk space temporarily.

options.label: Delete outright once verified
options.description: After the arm replacements are installed and every binary is confirmed resolving to /opt/homebrew, rm -rf the old trees in the same session. Reclaims space immediately, not reversible without reinstalling.

options.label: Use brew's own uninstaller
options.description: Run the official Homebrew uninstall script scoped to /usr/local for the brew tree, and anaconda-clean for conda. Slower and more interactive, but uses each tool's supported removal path rather than rm -rf.
